text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000064 bills 99215 far above risk-adjusted expectation, mostly on patients with 0-1 chronic conditions, but records are too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is concerning. The 99215 share is elevated in every complexity stratum, including patients with zero conditions, and most 99215s fall on low-complexity patients. Sampled low-complexity 99215s carry simple diagnoses such as URI, UTI, rash, back pain and follow-up codes (e.g., C0031707, C0032123, C0032149, C0031749), a pattern consistent with upcoding. The documentation points the other way but is too thin to settle it. Only 4 documented 99215 claims came back, all supported at high MDM, and one of those (C0031881) is a genuinely complex patient. Four of 9 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review had no lab or test line on the claim, which is weak evidence of templated or inflated notes. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed, compare note content against the simple diagnoses billed, and check for cloned language across notes."}
